chunks: From him, from his father, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, raising it to Abu Baseer who said:

I entered upon Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) in the year in which Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) passed away, so I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! What is the matter that you slaughtered a ram, and so and so slaughtered a camel?'

So he (peace be upon him) said: 'O Abu Muhammad! Nuh (peace be upon him) was in the ship, and therein was what Allah willed, and the ship was under Command, so it performed the Tawaf of the House, and it is the Tawaf of the women, and Nuh (peace be upon him) had freed its way.'

So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, Revealed unto the mountains: 'I shall be Placing the ship of Nuh, My servant, upon a mountain from you.' So they prolonged themselves and rose high, and the Judy humbled itself, and it is a mountain in your presence. So the ship struck the mountain with its keel.
So Nuh (peace be upon him) said at that: 'O Mary Atqin', and it is in Assyrian: 'O Lord! Keep it well'.
He (the narrator) said, 'So I thought Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) was applying it to his own case'.

key_terms.الْجُودِيُّ: Mount Judy, the mountain where the Ark rested
key_terms.طَوَافُ النِّسَاءِ: The Tawaf of the women, referring to the circumambulation of the Ark around the Kaaba
key_terms.عَرَّضَ بِنَفْسِهِ: Applied it to his own case / made a subtle reference to himself

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam Musa al-Kadhim slaughter a ram while others slaughtered camels?
ai.summary: In the year of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq's death, Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS) uses the story of Noah's Ark to illustrate the virtue of humility (tawadu'), contrasting the pride of Mount Judi with the self-effacement of the mountain that received the Ark. This narrative serves as a subtle allegory for his own political and spiritual stance during the turbulent period following his father's passing, emphasizing that true elevation comes from divine command and humility rather than worldly status. The slaughter of the ram is thus contextualized not merely as a ritual but as a commemorative act linking the Imam's lineage to the prophetic tradition of divine favor bestowed upon the humble.

en.hubeali: From him, from his father, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, raising it to Abu Baseer who said,

‘I went over to Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup> during the year in which Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> had passed away, so I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! What is the matter that you<sup>asws</sup> slaughtered a ram, and so and so slaughtered a camel?’

So heasws said: ‘O Abu Muhammad! Nuhas was in the ship, and therein was what Allahazwj so Desired, and the ship was under Command, so it performed the Tawāf of the House (Kabah), and it is the Tawaaf Al-Nisa, and Nuhas had freed its way.

So Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Revealed unto the mountain: “I<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> shall be Placing the ship of Nuh<sup style="font-weight: normal">as</sup>, My<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> servant, upon a mountain from you”. So they (the mountains) prolonged themselves to be higher, and the (Mount) Judy humbled itself, and it is a mountain in your presence. So the ship struck the mountain with its keel.
So Nuhas said during that: ‘O Māry Atqin’, and it is in Assyrian (meaning): ‘O Lordazwj! Keep it well’.
He (the narrator) said, ‘So I thought Abu Al-Hassan<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> applying it his<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> own case’.
en.sarwar: 12. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from a number of his people from Ali ibn Asbat from al-Hassan ibn al-Jahm from abu al-Hassan al- Rida (a.s.) who has said the following:
“Humbleness is a form of behavior that one expects others to behave that way toward him.”
“In another Hadith the narrator asked, ‘What is the definition of humbleness for which a servant (of Allah) could be considered humble?’

The Imam said, ‘There are several levels of humbleness. One is to know the value of one’s soul to place it at the position that it deserves with a peaceful heart and should not love to behave toward others in a way different from what he loves others to behave toward him. If he may find an evil behavior he should change it to a virtuous one. Those who suppress their anger are safe from people and Allah loves those who do good. ’”
